Sara —

Really helpful context and thanks for the attachments. High-level guidance below (concise so procurement can read quickly):

1) Batching vs KV/prefix caching
- For a read-heavy claims summarization flow with many repeated prompts (same templates, different records), prioritize KV/prefix caching first. It yields the best per-token cost reduction for tail-latency-sensitive requests because it avoids re-encoding prefix tokens.
- Batching is effective for throughput spikes (e.g., end-of-day claim batches) but increases median latency; recommend enabling dynamic batching with a 30–50ms window and a max batch size tuned during pilot.

2) Quantization recommendations
- If you need near-production quality and minimal regressions: start with mixed FP16/int8 (we call it fp16+llm-int8) per our model profiles; this preserves most quality at ~1.6x speedup.
- Aggressive int8-only quantization gains more cost savings but has higher QA risk on hallucination-sensitive prompts. We can run a short eval set during week 1 of the pilot to measure delta and decide whether to move to int8.

3) Commercial / pilot concession (ballpark)
- 6-week pilot: 150k token credits (covers dev + validation) + 20% credit match on billable usage up to $8k — intended to accelerate evaluation.
- We can include a single technical support engagement (4 engineer-hours) to tune batching/cache parameters.

Next steps: if that looks reasonable I can loop in Pricing and send a one-page pilot addendum (DocuSign) + a short ops checklist for the implementation runbook.

I'll also loop Dylan & Marcus to confirm capacity and whether we should include a small SLA carveout for the pilot.
